etymologies.etymologyHTML: From dis- +‎ like.

definitions.definition: An attitude or a feeling of distaste or aversion.
(usually in the plural) Something that a person dislikes (has or feels aversion to).
(Internet) An individual vote showing disapproval of, or lack of support for, something posted on the Internet.
(obsolete, transitive) To displease; to offend. In third-person only. [16th–19th c.]

quote.citation: 1603, Michel de Montaigne, chapter 12, in John Florio, transl., The Essayes […], book II, London:  […]  Val[entine] Simmes for Edward Blount […], →OCLC:
quote.text: customes and conceipts differing from mine, doe not so much dislike [translating desplaisent] me, as instruct me […].

definitions.definition: (transitive) To have a feeling of aversion or antipathy towards; not to like. [from 16th c.]

quote.citation: 1951 December, Michael Robbins, “John Francis's "History of the English Railway"”, in Railway Magazine, page 800:
quote.text: In the thick of the railway controversies of his day, Francis naturally had his prejudices. It seems that he cordially disliked the aristocracy in general.

definitions.definition: (Internet) To leave a vote to show disapproval of, or lack of support for, something posted on the Internet.
